title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck proved Corollary 3 by reducing the equality f = g to agreement on rational points. That reduction uses the fact that a K-point gives a conjugacy class of sections. This page states the injectivity theorem behind it, now called the injectivity half of the section conjecture.

Theorem 3. Let K be a field finitely generated over Q, with algebraic closure K̄, and let X be a geometrically connected K-scheme of finite type. Assume one of two hypotheses:
(i) X embeds into a semi-abelian variety G (an extension of an abelian variety by a torus); or
(ii) X is an elementary Artin neighbourhood, i.e. a tower of elementary fibrations in affine curves, whose geometric fibres are never P^1 or A^1. G_m fibres and hyperbolic fibres are therefore allowed.

Notation. Let E_{X/K} be the canonical (outer) extension 1 → π1(X̄) → E_{X/K} → Gal(K̄/K) → 1. Let Ẽ_{X/K} be its pushout to π1(X̄)^ab = H1(X̄).

Claim (completed on the next page): the following two canonical maps are injective.
(*) X(K) → {π1(X̄)-conjugacy classes of sections of E_{X/K}}.
(**) X(K) → {conjugacy classes of sections of Ẽ_{X/K}}. Since the kernel is abelian, these classes form a torsor under H^1(K, H1(X̄)).

Proof plan (next page):
1. (**) implies (*), because (*) factors through (**).
2. Under (i), with a base point, functoriality reduces to the case X = G.
3. The map then becomes the Kummer homomorphism G(K) → H^1(K, T̂G), with T̂G = lim_n nG.
4. Taking the Kummer sequences 0 → nG → G → G → 0 and passing to the limit gives lim_n G(K)/nG(K) ↪ lim_n H^1(K, nG).
5. Injectivity therefore reduces to ∩_n nG(K) = 0. This holds because G(K) is finitely generated for K finitely generated over Q (Mordell–Weil–Lang–Néron, plus finite generation for tori).

Marginal note: the result should hold for K finitely generated over its prime field in any characteristic, provided X is proper and smooth.

Purpose: this is the rigidity/injectivity input for the anabelian program. Points are determined by their Galois sections. Hom-type statements (Cor. 3: f = g if they induce the same map on fundamental groups) are then reduced to it.
errors: Hypothesis (ii) is not covered by the sketched proof. The next page reduces (**) to the case where X is a semi-abelian group. An elementary Artin neighbourhood need not embed in a semi-abelian variety. Its generalized (Serre) Albanese map need not be injective. Moreover H1(X̄) can differ from the Tate module of the generalized Albanese by finite torsion coming from NS/Pic torsion. So injectivity of (**) under (ii) is unjustified and plausibly false in general. For (ii) one would instead argue for (*) by induction along the fibration. Even that needs care when comparing conjugacy classes in the fibre group, since the centre is nontrivial for G_m-fibres.

The marginal positive-characteristic extension is too optimistic as stated. With p-power torsion and the trace part of Lang–Néron, the Kummer map can fail to be injective on the p-part unless the full étale/fppf π1 is used carefully. This is only a hesitant marginal note.
Minor: a rational point (or a degree-1 0-cycle) is needed for the Albanese embedding. When X(K) is empty the statement is vacuous, so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Injectivity of the section map X(K) → conjugacy classes of sections of π1(X) → Gal_K, for K finitely generated over Q
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings, 1983); written proofs in e.g. Stix, Rational Points and Arithmetic of Fundamental Groups (LNM 2054), and Nakamura/Tamagawa-era literature
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983), where the section conjecture and its injectivity part are discussed

ideas.what: Reduction of injectivity to the abelianized extension and to the Kummer map for semi-abelian varieties, using finite generation of G(K)
ideas.modern_name: Kummer map G(K) → H^1(K, TG) injective via Mordell–Weil–Lang–Néron (no nontrivial divisible elements)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard argument (Lang–Néron; folklore in anabelian geometry; e.g. Stix's book)

ideas.what: Allowing X to be an elementary Artin neighbourhood with non-rational fibres (G_m fibres permitted), as an alternative to embedding in a semi-abelian variety
ideas.modern_name: Section map for good (K(π,1)) neighbourhoods / elementary fibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin (SGA4 XI) for the neighbourhoods; their K(π,1) role is emphasised in Grothendieck's letter to Faltings
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings mentions elementary neighbourhoods in an anabelian context

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates injectivity of both the full and the abelianized section maps for elementary Artin neighbourhoods. He then proves only the semi-abelian case, so the Artin-neighbourhood case of (**) is left unjustified and is likely false. Injectivity for (*) in that generality via fibration induction is a modest, known-in-spirit thread.
missed.quote: ou que X est une variété élémentaire d'Artin, à fibres types géom. distinctes de la droite projective et de la droite affine
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor historical detail. It shows Grothendieck pushing injectivity toward higher-dimensional K(π,1) neighbourhoods, including G_m fibres, but nothing substantively new for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard injectivity of the section map via Kummer theory and Mordell–Weil, already known from the Faltings letter and later expositions. The only slight interest is the formulation for elementary Artin neighbourhoods with G_m fibres allowed, and the tentative positive-characteristic remark.
transcription_corrections: 'Supposons [?] X est une variété élémentaire' is more likely 'ou que X soit/est une variété élémentaire d'Artin', an alternative hypothesis inside the parenthesis.
'(et se plonge dans une extension d'une VA par un tore' opens a parenthesis that closes after 'droite affine)'.
In (*), the inserted '$\pi(\bar X)$-' modifies 'conjugaison': 'classes de π(X̄)-conjugaison des scindages'.
'distinctes' is preceded by the inserted 'géom.' (geometric fibre types).
